H1_seed_disentanglement.reason: P3 seed averaging gains 0.00446 over the best member, but the algebraic seed-variance share is only 7.7% of consensus MSE; error rankings are shared across families (signed-error correlation 0.86-0.93). Seed noise changes the level a little, not the hard-core membership.

H2_label_structure_coverage.reason: J's exact full typed path content covers 99.6% of valid path occurrences and still does not beat P3; the label-size curve cannot plausibly reverse that. Radius-2 signatures are 97.2% covered by unique type; the residual signal is rare support/composition, not a global shortage of labels.

H3_readout_interface_dilution.reason: P3 Null grouping feeds every bond n_b * graph-mean junction moments, so local junction identity is discarded. Error is concentrated in molecules with unseen radius-2 environments (25% of rows, 50% of absolute error) and ring-rich local environments, while adding path content at the atom input (J) or full global trunks (M/S) does not fix it.

H4_target_tail.reason: y<=-3 is 6.5% of rows but 16.2% of absolute error; the radius-2 effect survives within y>-3 (0.134 vs 0.048), so the tail contributes but does not explain the hard core.

platform_answer: The 0.076 plateau is a shared, heavy-tailed hard-core problem: the worst 25% of molecules carry 69% of absolute error, 25% of molecules with unseen radius-2 local environments carry 50%, and all seven fixed checkpoints fail the same molecules. It is not primarily seed disagreement and not a shortage of path labels.
